resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 CCC wooden tower was the first on the site; the 1964 steel tower replaced it and is the structure now standing, which explains the record's 1964 date.
Register gives 3,705 ft (1,129 m) and the Forest Service 3,704 ft; the difference is one foot and the record's 1129.3 m follows the register.

notes_for_editor: Current use is well sourced by the Forest Service release of September 8, 2026: the cab and campsite are open for rental, booked on Recreation.gov, with the 2027 season April 15 to November 30. The Recreation.gov listing itself was not read, so check rates and dates there before publishing. Open disagreements, left in the story: location (register says east of Cowen; Forest Service says about 12 miles south of Cowen) and cab size (register 14 by 14 ft; 2023 news 12 by 13 ft). The register's 80-foot height is also used by the 2023 news report, so it is treated as settled. The record's access 'unknown' is now given as public (rental). No corrections proposed. No photos added: the register's May 2022 photo is credited to an individual with no licence shown. The rental release does not say whether the tower itself may be climbed, so the story does not advise climbing it.
